title: Perceptions as Hypotheses: Saccades as Experiments
authors: Karl Friston, Rick Adams, Laurent Perrinet, Michael Breakspear
core_idea: Under active inference, perception and action both minimize the same free-energy functional — the brain literally acts to test its perceptual hypotheses.
why_it_matters: The founding statement that one objective (expected free energy) can drive perception, planning, and curiosity — a template for agents that need no separate reward function. Kept short here; neuroscience context in domain 04.

title: World Models
authors: David Ha, Jürgen Schmidhuber
core_idea: Train a tiny VAE world model and an RNN predictor of its latent dynamics, then evolve a small controller inside hallucinated dreams instead of the real environment.
why_it_matters: First striking demonstration that a *learned internal simulator* can be the training ground for behavior — the conceptual seed of Dreamer and of all latent-imagination agents.

title: Learning Latent Dynamics for Planning from Pixels (PlaNet) / [2020] Dream to Control (Dreamer)
authors: Danijar Hafner, Timothy Lillicrap, et al.
core_idea: PlaNet learns a recurrent state-space model from pixels and plans in it; Dreamer makes it sample-efficient by backpropagating value through imagined trajectories (latent imagination) with a replay of only real interactions.
why_it_matters: Converts RL from trial-and-error in reality to *learning inside a learned model* — the efficiency route to agents that cannot afford millions of real mistakes.

title: Scaling Active Inference
authors: Alex Tschantz, Beren Millidge, Anil K. Seth, Christopher L. Buckley
core_idea: Deep active-inference agents (expected free energy = extrinsic value + epistemic value) match or beat model-free RL on standard domains and solve tasks RL cannot without reward shaping.
why_it_matters: Shows active inference is an engineering-viable alternative to reward-based RL — intrinsic curiosity falls out of the objective rather than being bolted on.

title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models (DreamerV3)
authors: Danijar Hafner, Jurgis Pasukonis, Jimmy Ba, Timothy Lillicrap
core_idea: A single fixed hyperparameter set masters 150+ tasks across benchmarks, and becomes the first agent to collect a Minecraft diamond from scratch, with no human data.
why_it_matters: First evidence that one world-model-based learner can scale across wildly different domains — a concrete counter-proposal to "one benchmark per specialized RL stack".

title: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence (JEPA position paper)
authors: Yann LeCun
core_idea: An architecture blueprint (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) in which agents predict in *abstract representation space*, not pixels, using a hierarchy of world models plus a configurator and intrinsic cost.
why_it_matters: The most detailed published alternative to the generative-next-token path: prediction without generation, planning in latent space, energy-based inference — and it now anchors a real research program (I-JEPA, V-JEPA).

title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (I-JEPA)
authors: Mahmoud Assran, Quentin Duval, Ishan Misra, et al. (Meta)
core_idea: Predict representations of masked image regions from other regions, in embedding space — no pixel reconstruction, no hand-crafted augmentations.
why_it_matters: First large-scale working instance of LeCun's blueprint: representation learning by latent prediction beats generative and contrastive pipelines, validating "predict abstractions, not pixels".

title: Revisiting Feature Prediction for Learning Visual Representations from Video (V-JEPA)
authors: Adrien Bardes, Quentin Garrido, Jean Ponce, et al. (Meta)
core_idea: Extends JEPA to video: predict latent features of temporally masked frames; the model develops intuitive physics (object permanence, action prediction) without labels.
why_it_matters: Moves world models toward the pretraining-scale regime — a video-prediction substrate that downstream agents and robotics stacks can build on.

title: Hybrid Computing Using a Neural Network with Dynamic External Memory (DNC)
authors: Alex Graves, Greg Wayne, Ivo Danihelka, et al. (DeepMind)
core_idea: A neural controller with a differentiable, addressable external memory matrix it learns to read, write, and allocate — inference and manipulation by pure gradient descent.
why_it_matters: Memory as an explicit architectural component (not emergent state) — the ancestor of RAG indexes, agent episodic stores, and test-time-memory architectures.

title: Learning to Reinforcement Learn
authors: Jane X. Wang, Zeb Kurth-Nelson, Dhruva Tirumala, et al. (DeepMind)
core_idea: An RNN meta-trained across many tasks learns implicit RL algorithms in its recurrent dynamics — including exploration strategies adapted to each new task at test time.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates that learning-to-learn can emerge in weights + activation state rather than hand-designed updates; the pre-LLM statement of "pretraining then adapting" for decision-making.

title: HyperNetworks
authors: David Ha, Andrew Dai, Quoc V. Le
core_idea: One network generates the weights of another, so model structure itself becomes a learned, dynamically adaptable function of context.
why_it_matters: Weights stop being fixed parameters and become *state* — the conceptual root of fast weights, hypernetwork adapters, and test-time weight adaptation.

title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks (MAML)
authors: Chelsea Finn, Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine
core_idea: Optimize initial parameters explicitly so that a few gradient steps on a new task yield good performance — learn an initialization, not a solution.
why_it_matters: The canonical formalization of "learn to adapt in k steps"; the reference point every sample-efficient-adaptation scheme (including LLM-tuning-as-meta-learning analogies) is measured against.

title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
authors: Hubert Ramsauer, Bernhard Schäfl, Johannes Lehner, et al. (Hochreiter group)
core_idea: Transformer attention is mathematically equivalent to one update step of a modern (exponential-capacity) Hopfield network retrieving a stored pattern.
why_it_matters: Reframes attention as *associative memory retrieval* — connecting transformers to the Hopfield energy-based lineage (domain 01) and licensing energy-based, memory-centric alternatives to softmax attention.

title: The "Echo State" Approach to Analysing and Training Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Herbert Jaeger
link: GMD Report 148, German National Research Center for Information Technology
core_idea: Keep a large random recurrent reservoir fixed and train only a linear readout — the "echo state" property makes the reservoir a fading memory of its input history.
why_it_matters: Established reservoir computing: dynamics as a fixed feature map, learning confined to a cheap output layer — the low-energy predecessor of today's frozen-backbone + small-adapter designs.

title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: Ricky T. Q. Chen, Yulia Rubanova, Jesse Bettencourt, David Duvenaud
core_idea: Define network depth as a continuous ODE solved by standard numerical integrators, with gradients via the adjoint method at constant memory cost.
why_it_matters: Makes *continuous time* a first-class modeling axis — the mathematical basis for liquid networks and for architectures that trade discrete layers for physical-time dynamics.

title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
authors: Bo Peng, Eric Alcaide, et al.
core_idea: An RNN that can be trained in parallel like a transformer (linear attention reformulated as a recurrence) and runs in constant memory at inference.
why_it_matters: Proof that recurrence and parallel training are not mutually exclusive — a streaming, deployable alternative to quadratic attention born in the open-source community.

title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models
authors: Michael Poli, Stefano Massaroli, Eric Nguyen, et al.
core_idea: Replace attention with long implicit convolutions gated by a small MLP, yielding subquadratic scaling to hundreds of thousands of context tokens.
why_it_matters: Showed the attention kernel itself is replaceable at language-model scale — the long-convolution branch of the post-transformer zoo that Mamba later overshadowed.

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
authors: Albert Gu, Tri Dao
core_idea: Make state-space parameters input-dependent (selective), so the model chooses what to remember or forget — transformer-class quality at linear time and constant per-token memory.
why_it_matters: The flagship non-transformer backbone: streaming/edge inference, million-token contexts, and DNA/audio modeling — and the template the whole 2024+ SSM ecosystem (Jamba, hybrid stacks) builds on.

title: xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory
authors: Maximilian Beck, Korbinian Pöppel, Markus Spanring, et al. (Hochreiter group)
core_idea: Modernizes the LSTM with exponential gating and matrix memory (sLSTM, mLSTM), restoring the classic cell's competitiveness with transformers and Mamba.
why_it_matters: The recurrence line did not die in 2017 — a direct counter-demonstration that gated recurrence, properly upgraded, belongs in the architecture search space.

title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
authors: Ziming Liu, Yixuan Wang, Sachin Vaidya, et al.
core_idea: Put learnable activation functions on edges (B-splines) instead of fixed activations on nodes, exploiting the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem.
why_it_matters: Small KANs discover symbolic, interpretable formulas where MLPs fit opaque surfaces — an architecture whose inductive bias points toward compositional and scientific discovery, not just benchmark loss.

title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States (TTT layers)
authors: Yu Sun, Xinhao Li, Karan Dalal, et al. (Stanford)
core_idea: Make the RNN hidden state itself a small neural network whose update rule is a step of self-supervised learning — the sequence layer literally trains its memory during the forward pass.
why_it_matters: Unifies fast weights, meta-learning, and long-context modeling: adaptation stops being a separate fine-tuning phase and becomes part of inference.

title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
authors: Ali Behrouz et al. (Google)
core_idea: A neural long-term memory module that *surprises-based* writes and forgets at test time, coordinated with short-term attention in a hybrid architecture that scales beyond 2M context.
why_it_matters: Memory management (what to store, when to forget) becomes an architectural, learned-in-place mechanism — a direct answer to the context-window economics of long-horizon agents.

title: Large Language Diffusion Models (LLaDA)
authors: Shen Nie, Fengqi Zhu, Chao Du, et al. (Ant Group, Renmin University)
core_idea: An 8B-parameter diffusion LM trained from scratch with masked-diffusion pretraining and instruction tuning that rivals LLaMA3-8B on many benchmarks.
why_it_matters: First convincing evidence that the *generative paradigm itself* (any-order parallel denoising vs left-to-right factorization) is swappable at language-model scale, with built-in infilling and controllability.

title: Commercial diffusion language models: Mercury and Gemini Diffusion
authors: Inception Labs; Google DeepMind
core_idea: Mercury (2025-02) ships the first commercial-scale diffusion LLM at 1000+ tokens/sec on H100s; Gemini Diffusion (2025-05) is Google DeepMind's research-preview diffusion model with comparable speed.
why_it_matters: Parallel diffusion decoding turns generation speed from a serial-token constraint into a hardware-parallel one — the first deployed crack in autoregressive orthodoxy.

title: Liquid Time-Constant Networks
authors: Ramin Hasani, Mathias Lechner, et al. (MIT)
core_idea: Neural ODEs whose time constants are states, so each neuron adapts its own clock to the input — closed-form variants (CfC) make them cheap enough for deployment.
why_it_matters: Networks that natively handle irregular sampling and time-warped streams (robotics, wearables, edge sensing) — where fixed-clock discrete stacks waste computation.

title: Networks of Spiking Neurons: The Third Generation of Neural Network Models
authors: Wolfgang Maass
core_idea: Neurons that communicate by discrete spikes are computationally more powerful than sigmoid units — even with the same analog noise — when time is used as a resource.
why_it_matters: The theoretical charter for event-driven, sparse, energy-cheap computation; every neuromorphic hardware claim descends from it. (Cross-ref domain 04 for the neuroscience side; not yet covered there as of 2026-10.)

title: Loihi: A Neuromorphic Manycore Processor with On-Chip Learning
authors: Mike Davies et al. (Intel)
core_idea: A 128-core chip with asynchronous spiking neurons and programmable on-chip plasticity rules, consuming milliwatts on workloads that cost GPUs watts.
why_it_matters: Physical proof that learning can run at 3-5 orders of magnitude lower energy than GPU training/inference — the hardware existence theorem for always-on embedded intelligence.

title: SpikeGPT: Generative Pre-trained Language Model with Spiking Neural Networks
authors: Rui-Jie Zhu, Qihang Zhao, Guoqi Li, Jason K. Eshraghian
core_idea: A GPT-style language model (up to 345M params) built on spiking RWKV neurons, generating text with binary event-driven activations at roughly 20x less energy than an equivalent dense model.
why_it_matters: The bridge paper: modern generative LLM architecture rendered in spiking form — connects the LLM world to neuromorphic hardware deployment rather than toy tasks.

title: DeepProbLog: Neural Probabilistic Logic Programming
authors: Robin Manhaeve, Sebastijan Dumančić, Angelika Kimmig, Thomas Demeester, Luc De Raedt
core_idea: Embed neural networks as probabilistic predicates inside a differentiable logic program, so gradients flow through logical inference itself.
why_it_matters: The cleanest mechanism for systematic compositionality: symbols guarantee rule structure while sub-symbolic nets supply perception — exactly the generalization pattern pure LLMs still miss.

title: The Neuro-Symbolic Concept Learner: Interpreting Scenes, Words, and Sentences from Natural Supervision
authors: Jiayuan Mao, Chuang Gan, Pushmeet Kohli, Joshua Tenenbaum, Jiajun Wu
core_idea: A visual parser turns pixels into object programs, a semantic parser turns questions into symbolic programs, and answering is program execution — no program annotations.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates human-like data efficiency and zero-shot recombination on VQA by splitting perception (neural) from reasoning (symbolic) — the architecture pattern behind 2024-25 neuro-symbolic ARC solvers.

title: Abandoning Objectives: Evolution Through the Search for Novelty Alone
authors: Joel Lehman, Kenneth O. Stanley
core_idea: Searching only for behavioral novelty — with no objective function at all — sometimes finds solutions that objective-driven search never reaches (e.g., the deceptive-maze robot).
why_it_matters: Formalizes that objectives can actively mislead: stepping stones to intelligence may only be discoverable by open-ended, novelty-seeking search — a design principle for generating what we cannot specify.

title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning
authors: Tim Salimans, Jonathan Ho, Xi Chen, et al. (OpenAI)
core_idea: Black-box evolution of policy parameters, parallelized across thousands of gradient-free workers, matches deep RL on MuJoCo while sidestepping backprop-through-time entirely.
why_it_matters: Learning without gradients is embarrassingly parallel and non-differentiable-stack-friendly — the fallback optimizer for world models, agents, and hardware where gradients do not flow.

title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET)
authors: Rui Wang, Joel Lehman, et al.
core_idea: Endlessly generate new environments and their solvers together, transferring agents between paired challenges to keep difficulty at each learner's frontier.
why_it_matters: The first working engine of open-ended co-evolution of tasks and solutions — an automatic curriculum generator, and a concrete answer to "where does an endless training signal come from?".

title: Emergence of Linguistic Communication from Referential Games
authors: Angeliki Lazaridou, Alexander Peysakhovich, Marco Baroni (with 2016 antecedents)
core_idea: Two agents invent a discrete language to solve referential games; grounded, compositional-ish protocols emerge from pure cooperation pressure, but drift toward non-human languages without inductive biases.
why_it_matters: The experimental base camp for emergent communication: tells you exactly which pressures (grounding, population, ease) make shared symbolic systems arise — and which make them alien.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
authors: Joon Sung Park, Joseph O'Brien, Carrie Cai, et al. (Stanford)
core_idea: 25 LLM agents with memory streams, reflection, and planning in a sandbox town produce believable social behavior (party planning, relationship formation) evaluated by human raters.
why_it_matters: The founding demo of society-scale simulation: LLMs as substrate for social-science experiments, agent economies, and synthetic populations — collective intelligence built from generative individuals.

title: Multi-agent LLM ecosystems: swarms, MCP, agent-to-agent protocols
authors: ecosystem development (no single paper)
core_idea: A practical stack crystallizes around standard tool protocols (MCP, 2024), agent swarms/orchestration frameworks, and emerging agent-to-agent communication formats across vendors.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent intelligence is becoming *infrastructure* rather than research demo — standard interfaces let heterogeneous agents compose, which is the precondition for agent economies and collective systems that outgrow any single model.

title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
authors: Eric Zelikman, Yuhuai Wu, Jesse Mu, Noah D. Goodman (Stanford)
core_idea: Generate rationales, keep only those that produce correct final answers, fine-tune on them, and re-generate — reasoning ability bootstraps itself upward from a few seeds.
why_it_matters: The origin loop of LLM self-improvement: the STaR pattern (generate, filter by outcome, train, repeat) is the direct ancestor of rejection-sampling fine-tuning and RLVR-era reasoning training.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
authors: Timo Schick, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Roberto Dessì, et al. (Meta)
core_idea: A model self-annotates where inserting an API call (calculator, search, QA) would reduce its own perplexity, then fine-tunes on those insertions — tool use learned, not prompted.
why_it_matters: The model becomes the dispatcher that decides *when* computation should leave its weights — the learning-side foundation of function calling and of agents that offload exact work to tools.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
authors: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Beck Labash, et al.
core_idea: Agents that fail a task store a *verbal* self-diagnosis in episodic memory and retry with that lesson in context — episodic control implemented in language instead of weights.
why_it_matters: Cheap, gradient-free self-improvement: converting execution feedback into natural-language policy updates is now the standard inner loop of serious agent frameworks.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
authors: Guanzhi Wang, Yuqi Xie, Yunfan Jiang, et al. (NVIDIA, Caltech)
core_idea: An LLM agent in Minecraft writes its own actions as code, verifies them, and stores verified skills in a growing skill library that compounds across tasks without any gradient updates.
why_it_matters: The skill-library pattern: continual learning as *accumulated executable artifacts* — the most copied mechanism for making agents improve monotonically in open worlds.

title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
authors: Andrew Zhao, Yiran Wu, Yang Yue, et al. (Tsinghua LeapLab)
core_idea: One model both *proposes* tasks (to maximize its own learnability) and solves them, verified by a code executor — AlphaZero-style self-play for reasoning with zero external data.
why_it_matters: A working escape from the human-data bottleneck: the training signal is generated and checked by machine, pointing at open-ended self-improvement loops (and their unsupervised-error risks).

title: OpenAI o3 on ARC-AGI: reasoning models crack (part of) the generality benchmark
authors: OpenAI (system milestone)
core_idea: o3, trained with RL on verifiable tasks plus large test-time search, scored 75.7% (87.5% with 172x compute) on ARC-AGI-Pub — the first big jump on the benchmark that had resisted a decade of approaches.
why_it_matters: Evidence that Chollet's skill-acquisition framing (domain 01) responds to RL + test-time search — while costing enormous compute per task, showing "generality" and "efficiency" are still far from joint. System-scale evidence, flagged as such.

title: ARC-AGI-2: the persistent holdout
authors: ARC Prize Foundation (benchmark milestone)
core_idea: A redesigned ARC suite targeting the efficiency gap — tasks tuned so humans still solve most while frontier reasoning models score in the single to low double digits at release.
why_it_matters: Even o3-class systems only partially crack ARC-AGI-1 at extreme cost, and ARC-AGI-2 re-opens the gap: a live yardstick separating "skill at scale" from general, *sample-efficient* intelligence (Chollet 2019, domain 01).

title: AI Safety via Debate
authors: Geoffrey Irving, Paul Christiano, Dario Amodei (OpenAI)
core_idea: Two adversarial AI debaters with a human judging only the transcript can, in principle, supervise capabilities beyond the judge's own — amplifying oversight instead of capability alone.
why_it_matters: The core mechanism candidate for supervising smarter-than-human systems: supervision scales with computation spent on debate, not with judge expertise.

title: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
authors: Samuel R. Bowman et al.
core_idea: A unified evaluation suite (weak-strong pairings, sandwiching, debate, market-making) for the concrete question: can weak overseers extract truthful behavior from stronger models?
why_it_matters: Turns oversight from philosophy into benchmark engineering — defines the measurable race between model capability and our ability to check it.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
authors: Collin Burns, Pavel Izmailov, Jan Hendrik Kirchner, et al. (OpenAI)
core_idea: Fine-tuning a strong model on labels from a much weaker one recovers most of the strong model's capability — and sometimes beats the weak supervisor's own ceiling.
why_it_matters: Empirical hope that humans can keep steering superhuman models via weak signals (if generalization conditions hold) — the working hypothesis behind 2025-26 oversight plans for self-improving systems.
